title: I think Jaws is Spielberg’s best film

commenti.body:
Personally, I like how the themes foreshadowed how the COVID pandemic played out in the US. 

“Hey look, there’s a threat to public safety.”

“But we can’t close anything, we might lose money!”

Predicted problem gets worse. 

Businesses forced to close/adjust eventually anyway. 


Plus there is Quint’s great monologue about the Indianapolis. There’s a lot going on in the film, and I hate to say one or another is someone’s best, but it’s definitely a great film.

I watched Jaws recently for the first time in probably twenty years. I completely agree with you. I was shocked by how well it held up. Especially when you consider how revolutionary and frankly avant garde some of the camera movements were at the time. 

In terms of building tension and suspense, this is Spielberg at his finest. 

The one moment holding this film back is the shark at the end. It looks ridiculous. But the rest of the film is so masterfully crafted that it allows me to overlook what would be a film-wrecker of a lesser film.

I agree 100%. I love most of his stuff pre-2000 but nothing comes close to Jaws. Maybe Raiders, but Jaws is just the better film. 

It is scary, adventurous, funny, sad. It can seamlessly move from beat to beat. Robert Shaw is probably the best actor that Spielberg has ever worked with and he pulls no punches. Just an excellent film
That’s a great point, never thought about the Covid parallel. And agreed on Quint’s monologue, outstanding.
Yeah the camerawork was very ahead of its time, even Scorsese wasn’t using those stylistic shots just yet.  The vertigo dolly zoom on the beach is classic.
